--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.personalized_pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Calculate Personalized PageRank with a custom restart distribution. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.personalized_pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: >- Calculate Personalized PageRank with a custom restart distribution. title: >- [Graph.personalized_pagerank()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Calculate Personalized PageRank with a custom restart distribution. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Calculate Personalized PageRank with a custom restart distribution. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L50266-L50444){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.personalized_pagerank( personalization, damping=0.85, max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Personalized PageRank](../assets/graphs/personalized-pagerank.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The shared seven-node graph with the seed A (node id 1) outlined, every node shaded by PageRank whose random surfer always restarts at A. Rank stays near the seed, A 0.26, C 0.23 and B 0.20, and fades along the strip to F 0.05 and G 0.02." width="100%"} Unlike standard PageRank where the random surfer teleports uniformly to any node, Personalized PageRank teleports back to seed nodes with probabilities given by `personalization`. This makes it the primary method for gene prioritization in genome-wide association studies (GWAS): seed nodes are GWAS hits, and the resulting scores rank candidate genes by network proximity to those hits. The scores are computed by power iteration. At each step a surfer follows a random outgoing edge with probability `damping=` and otherwise jumps back to a seed, picked in proportion to its personalization value. A node with no outgoing edges sends all of its rank back to the seeds. The resulting score of a node is the long-run fraction of time the surfer spends there, so nodes that are close to the seeds and reachable along many paths score highest. Typical uses besides gene prioritization: - "related items" ranking: which nodes matter most from the point of view of one node or a small set of nodes - local community detection around a seed set - comparing the influence of different seed sets on the same network In directed graphs the surfer only moves along edge direction; in undirected graphs it can move either way. Edge weights are not used: every outgoing edge is equally likely. `random_walk_with_restart()` computes the same scores with `restart_prob = 1 - damping`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [personalization]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[Union[int, str], float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping seed nodes, as integer IDs or string labels, to restart probabilities. Values are normalized internally, so they don't need to sum to 1. Nodes not in the dictionary have zero restart probability. Use a single entry for one seed, or several entries with larger values for seeds you trust more. Integer IDs that are not in the graph are ignored, and an unknown label raises an error. [damping]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.85]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Probability of following an edge (vs. teleporting back to a seed). Higher values let the walk spread further from the seeds. Typical range: `0.5`-`0.95`. The default is `0.85`. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of power-iteration steps. The default is `100`, which is enough for the default `damping=` on most graphs; values of `damping=` close to `1` converge more slowly and may need more. If the limit is reached, the current scores are returned without warning. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance. Iteration stops once the summed absolute change in all scores (the L1 norm of the change) between two steps falls below this value. The default is `1e-6`; smaller values give more precise scores at the cost of more iterations. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name for storing scores in the node DataFrame. Defaults to `"personalized_pagerank"`. An existing column with this name is overwritten. Use different names to keep results from several seed sets side by side. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, returns the score dictionary without writing anything to the graph. If `False` (default), stores scores in the node DataFrame and returns self for chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to scores (sum to `1.0`). Otherwise returns self. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `personalization=` is empty or its values do not sum to a positive number. ::: ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~pagerank`) : The same walk, restarting anywhere. [](`~random_walk_with_restart`) : The same computation, parameterized by `restart_prob=`. [](`~heat_diffusion`) : Spread a signal from the seeds by diffusion instead. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Starting every restart from `GeneA` keeps most of the rank there. `GeneD` comes second, because it is reached both directly from `GeneA` and at the end of the longer path, and as a dead end it sends its rank straight back to `GeneA`. Lowering `damping=` makes the surfer restart more often, so the rank stays closer to the seed, and `GeneC`, two steps away, loses about half of its score: ::: {#de200bc0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("GeneA", "GeneB"), ("GeneB", "GeneC"), ("GeneC", "GeneD"), ("GeneA", "GeneD")], directed=True, ) ( graph.personalized_pagerank({"GeneA": 1.0}, attr_name="damping_85") .personalized_pagerank( {"GeneA": 1.0}, damping=0.5, attr_name="damping_50" ) .get_node_df() .select("label", "damping_85", "damping_50") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Following the money In `payments()`, suppose that Cruz has been flagged for fraud. Seeded at Cruz, the surfer follows the payments out of that account, so the accounts that score highest are the ones Cruz's money flows to: Ana and Ivy, then Jo, Kai and Lena down the chain. The Grocer scores high too, since so many payments end there. Plain PageRank, with no seed, ranks Ivy among the lowest, but seen from Cruz, Ivy ties for second: ::: {#60d6c6a4 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import polars as pl payments = ( ec.payments() .pagerank() .personalized_pagerank({"Cruz": 1.0}, attr_name="from_cruz") ) ( payments.get_node_df() .select("label", "from_cruz", "pagerank") .sort("from_cruz", descending=True) .head(8) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ### Where the money came from Reversing the payments sends the surfer back along them, to the accounts that paid Cruz. Ben and Ana, the rest of the ring, come first. Dee comes next, for a single payment of 60 to Ben: every payment counts the same, whatever its amount. The scores are drawn here on the payments as they were made: ::: {#e850b840 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} to_cruz = payments.reverse().personalized_pagerank( {"Cruz": 1.0}, return_dict=True ) payments.set_node_attrs("to_cruz", to_cruz).plot( color_by="to_cruz", label_by="label", seed=3 ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
